title: Circles: Chords, Angles, and the Magic of π

questions.question: What is the longest chord of a circle called?
questions.rationale: The diameter is a chord passing through the centre; at 2r it is the longest chord in the circle.

questions.question: Which of these is TRUE about the number π?
options: It changes with the circle's size
questions.rationale: π = C/d is the same constant for every circle and is irrational, so 22/7 is only a convenient approximation.

questions.question: An angle at the circumference of a circle standing on arc AB is 35°. What is the central angle AOB on the same arc?
questions.rationale: The central-angle theorem: the angle at the centre is twice any angle at the circumference standing on the same arc, so 2 × 35° = 70°.

questions.question: An angle inscribed in a semicircle measures:
questions.rationale: The angle in a semicircle is exactly 90° — it is the central-angle theorem with the centre angle of 180° halved.

questions.question: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral always:
questions.rationale: In a cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles are supplementary — 110° faces 70° — and each exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle.

questions.question: At the point of contact, a tangent to a circle is:
options: Equal in length to the diameter
questions.rationale: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact — the single most-used tangent fact in exams.

questions.question: Two tangents drawn to a circle from the same external point are:
questions.rationale: Two tangents from an external point are equal in length, which makes the triangle they form with the centre line symmetric.

questions.question: A circle has radius 7 cm. Using π ≈ 22/7, its circumference and area are:
With r = 7 cm and central angle θ = 90°, the arc length is:
questions.rationale: Arc = (θ/360) × 2πr = (90/360) × 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44/4 = 11 cm — a quarter of the circumference. (38.5 cm² is the sector's area.)

questions.question: The area of the annulus between concentric circles of radii 5 and 3 is:
questions.rationale: The annulus area is the difference of areas: π(5² − 3²) = π(25 − 9) = 16π — squares subtract, not the radii themselves.
